slice.candidate_identity: Ambiguous acknowledgement loss where exact current target readback does not contain the stable effect identity; one conditional current-blob CAS decision is allowed
slice.tested_scope: Abstract repository-content effect only: stable effect identity is embedded in the intended content, current target content/blob can be read exactly, one update may be conditioned on the observed current blob, and no independent durability/authority witness is available. This slice does not claim historical commit visibility after rewrite/overwrite, does not cover non-idempotent external side effects, and performs no O/protected-primary mutation, Work execution, hosted compute, finite-quota feature, paid service, scheduler mutation or public-source discovery.

bounded_cases.case: lost request was not committed; current target still equals observed predecessor and effect identity is absent
bounded_cases.result: one CAS against the exact current blob may establish the desired current repository state; if it succeeds, current-state convergence is achieved

bounded_cases.case: lost request was not committed; a concurrent writer changed current content before the reconciliation CAS
bounded_cases.result: the reconciler must bind to the newly read current blob; a later CAS conflict is terminal for this invocation and must be checkpointed rather than retried

bounded_cases.case: lost request committed, then another writer overwrote or reverted the target before reconciliation readback
bounded_cases.result: current effect absence can be observationally identical to a never-committed attempt; current target content/blob alone cannot prove historical non-commit

bounded_cases.case: lost request committed and effect remains present
bounded_cases.result: outside this leaf because exact stable-effect readback would classify it as already applied before any CAS

observations: Exact current target absence proves only that the effect is not present now; it does not prove the acknowledgement-lost request never committed historically.

A stable effect identity plus exact current readback and one current-blob CAS is sufficient for bounded current-state convergence of a pure/reconstructible repository-content effect when the CAS succeeds.

The same mechanism is insufficient to prove exactly-once historical commit count, to distinguish commit-then-overwrite from never-committed history, or to protect a non-idempotent external side effect.
A CAS conflict after the bounded decision is a recurring-open continuation, not evidence that either historical branch is resolved.
slice.inference: The ambiguous absent-target branch refines the already retained stable-effect-identity + exact-readback + conditional-CAS acknowledgement-loss family. It is not an exact-distinct dependency-elimination mechanism. Its positive guarantee is current-state convergence within the tested repository-content scope; historical commit-status disambiguation remains unresolved without an additional surviving witness.
slice.o_comparison: NOT_RUN because exact-family duplicate/boundary classification resolves this bounded leaf without consuming protected O semantics.

blocker: Historical commit status remains indistinguishable when the stable effect is absent from current target state and no independently surviving witness is available; same-authority overwrite/rewrite can erase the differentiating history.
exact_continuation: Next invocation fresh-bootstrap current manifest/lifecycle/root/downstream authority, reconstruct this exact predecessor, then execute only GITHUB-CONTENTS-ACK-LOSS-ABSENT-TARGET-COMMIT-HISTORY-DISAMBIGUATION-GATE-v1. Test whether reachable repository commit ancestry plus stable effect identity can distinguish never-committed from commit-then-overwritten after acknowledgement loss without an independent durability domain, while preserving zero Work/protected-primary/manual execution, zero finite quota, zero incremental cost and fail-closed behavior under history rewrite/GC. If existing role-local evidence already subsumes it, persist only the duplicate classification and advance one nonempty continuation; do not start a second leaf.
